title: Artificial Lawns in the Denver Metro | TIMELESS Grass & Greens
description: Where turf can go on a Denver-area lot: what your HOA can limit for your type of home, how seven cities treat back and front yards, and who pays toward it.
h1: Artificial lawns in the Denver Metro, placed where your HOA and city allow.
lede: Where turf can go turns on your home type, your back fence and your city's front-yard rule. We measure, draw a layout you approve and put the price in writing.
wins: Know what your HOA can limit for your type of home
A custom layout drawn to your city's yard limits
A lawn that needs no watering days

answer.question: Can I replace my lawn with artificial turf in the Denver metro?
answer.answer: Usually in the back yard, and sometimes part of the front. Colorado law stops an HOA banning nonvegetative turf in a detached home's back yard, though attached homes may be held to the rear yard. Cities add their own limits on top.

blocks.h2: What your HOA can limit depends on the kind of home you own.
blocks.takeaway: If your home is detached, Colorado law stops your HOA banning turf in the back yard. If it shares a wall with another unit, the HOA can still hold turf to the rear yard only.
paras: On a detached home, association guidelines must "not prohibit the use of nonvegetative turf grass in the backyard of a unit owner's property" (C.R.S. 38-33.3-106.5(1)(i.5)). The board still keeps its bona fide safety rules, its rules on fire buffers and defensible space, and its say over changes to existing grading and drainage. Out front, the statute has the board preapprove at least three water-wise garden designs. Those are plantings, not turf.

If your home shares one or more walls with another unit, a different subsection applies. The association "shall not prohibit" nonvegetative turf grass on property you're responsible for, but it can set design rules and "may restrict the installation of nonvegetative turf grass to rear yard locations only" (C.R.S. 38-33.3-106.5(1)(i)). The detached-home subsection says in terms that it does not apply to a condominium. In a condo, ask the association for its written turf rules before you plan anything.

SB23-178 set up this split between detached and attached homes. It was signed on 17 May 2023 and took effect on 7 August 2023 (Colorado session laws, chapter 207). FindLaw's copy of the statute, current as of 1 January 2025, carries the same wording, so cite the section when you ask your board for its position in writing. None of it binds your city: the covenant rule in C.R.S. 37-60-126(11) "does not supersede any subdivision regulation" of a municipality (C.R.S. 37-60-126). The Colorado HOA turf guide covers what to do if a board refuses anyway.

blocks.h2: A back yard beside a street or park needs a check in two cities.
blocks.takeaway: In Arvada and Westminster, turf may be off-limits in a back yard seen from or next to a street or park, so check a corner or park-side lot first.
paras: In Arvada, turf can be the main ground cover in a back or side yard only where it is "not in public view", and public view covers anything seen from streets, sidewalks, parks and trails. A putting green of up to 400 square feet is the exception (Arvada § 4-6-7-2). The rule reaches a change to an existing landscape, unless your subdivision was first built with nine or fewer single-family or duplex lots (Arvada § 4-6-3-1).

In Westminster, the regulations allow turf in single-family detached and duplex "yard areas not adjacent to a street, or public or private park or open space" (Westminster Landscape Regulations 2004). So in both cities, check a corner lot, or a yard that backs onto a park, before you plan turf. Add sidewalks and trails in Arvada, and open space in Westminster.

The other cities treat the back yard differently. Thornton's rules say turf is "allowed with no limitations" in rear and enclosed side yards (Thornton Water rules dated 1 January 2026). Brighton lists artificial turf among the materials a back yard may have (Brighton § 8.02), while its water-wise rules ask for living ground cover on at least 50% of the landscape area (Brighton § 8.04). Northglenn applies its turf rules to existing single-family yards and bars turf on slopes greater than six percent (Northglenn Municipal Code).

blocks.h2: Out front, most cities cap the share, and two keep a turf lawn off the street.
blocks.takeaway: Out front, Thornton caps turf at 25% and Brighton at 20%; ask Aurora Planning in writing what its 50% cap measures. Arvada and Westminster leave no room for a street-facing turf lawn.
paras: The step 2 rules leave no room for a turf lawn in a street-facing front yard in Arvada or Westminster. Westminster also wants 50% of a single-family front yard in vegetation (City of Westminster FAQ, April 2025).

Thornton caps turf at 25% of the landscape area in front and unenclosed side yards. You need a Minor Development Permit before installation, and living plants with the turf: one tree equivalent for the first 750 square feet, and half of one for each additional 250 square feet (Thornton Water).

Brighton limits turf to 20% of the frontage area of a detached house, duplex or row house (Brighton § 8.02). Its landscape standards apply to new development. They exempt improvements to a detached house or duplex that need no Site Improvement or Residential Design Review and aren't part of a larger subdivision plan, and improvements to existing development that don't increase building footprint or impervious surfaces by more than 10% (Brighton § 8.01). Ask Community Development which case your address is.

Lafayette wants live materials on at least 75% of the gross front yard, driveways excluded. The section is written for new development, but it also says a building permit application for an individual single-family home must comply with that front-yard rule (Lafayette § 26-19-5). Ask the Planning Division whether your project needs a permit that brings it in.

Aurora Water's drought page says residents may install artificial turf "subject to a 50% coverage maximum", in its answer on why it gives no rebate for converting a yard entirely to turf. It doesn't say what the 50% is measured against (Aurora Water). Get that answer from Aurora Planning in writing before you draw a front lawn.

blocks.h2: Your water provider sets the rebate and the watering rules.
blocks.takeaway: Denver Water's rebate excludes turf and its 2026 discounts are gone, but Thornton's pays toward turf replacing a high-water lawn. Either way, turf skips the establishment watering new sod still needs.
paras: Budget the lawn without a rebate unless your provider confirms one in writing. Denver Water's lawn-removal discount needs a plan for a water-wise landscape, and "artificial turf is not allowed". A notice dated 28 March 2026 says its 2026 discounts have all been allocated (Denver Water). Thornton Water is the exception: its 2026 rebate pays toward turf that replaces high-water lawn on an existing lot. The water rebates guide covers Aurora, Erie, Highlands Ranch and the rest.

If you're weighing new sod instead, check establishment watering first. On 26 August 2026 Denver Water's board ended the lawn watering season, banning lawn watering and all spray irrigation after 30 September. Its watering rules also say establishment permits for new seed or sod "will not be available after Sept. 30 until further notice" (Denver Water). Aurora Water's drought page, read on 12 September 2026, lists Stage 1 rules that say "No new cool-weather turf can be installed" (Aurora Water).

Turf arrives green and needs no establishment watering or assigned days, though a rinse still takes some water. Drought stages change, so confirm the current rules with the provider named on your bill before you choose between sod and turf.

faq.q: Does turf count toward my city's planting requirement?
faq.a: Not in Lafayette. Its code says artificial grasses "shall not be used in any manner to satisfy the requirements" of its landscaping regulations (Lafayette § 26-19-5). Westminster's regulations say artificial turf can't be substituted for required plant materials unless they approve it (City of Westminster). Plan the planting beds and the lawn together.

faq.q: Are these city rules about to change?
faq.a: Two are being rewritten. Lafayette's schedule, updated 8 September 2026, set the council's final vote on a new land use code for 15 September 2026 (Lafayette Listens), so ask the Planning Division which code applies when you apply. Westminster's landscape rules date from 2004 and are being updated in a Unified Development Code, which a city presentation dated 2 March 2026 still calls proposed (City of Westminster). The city's FAQ says the updated rules apply to new development and are not retroactive (City of Westminster).

faq.q: Is artificial turf banned in Colorado?
faq.a: Not on a single-family lot. From 1 January 2026, state law stops local governments allowing artificial turf on commercial, institutional and industrial property, HOA common property, street rights-of-way, parking lots and medians (SB24-005). As amended, that rule covers nonfunctional artificial turf in new development or redevelopment projects, and from 1 January 2028 it also reaches multifamily properties with more than 12 dwelling units (HB25-1113). Your city and HOA can still limit turf at home. The Colorado turf law guide has the detail.

faq.q: My city isn't one of these. Where do I start?
faq.a: With its planning office. Ask whether turf may go in front, side and back yards, whether there's a share or slope limit, and whether you need a permit. Get the reply in writing, and check your water provider's rules separately.

faq.q: What should I bring to the free visit?
faq.a: Your HOA's written position, any reply from your city and the name of your water provider. We measure the area and check the ground, then draw a custom layout to those limits for you to approve before work starts. The artificial lawn service sets out the installation, and the Denver metro page covers the other turf we install here.
